learning: Iterations 5 and 8 showed that wheel_radius steps of 0.005 m raised s-bend progress by about 0.003 with max_error held. Mass (iteration 6) and track (iteration 7) both lowered progress. If max_error exceeds 0.069 at 0.044 m, speed has reached its useful limit at this controller setting, and the next step is a controller change for the faster robot, not more geometry.
notes: Complete package for the Builder's wheel_radius 0.044 m step on the iteration 8 best state. The controller is unchanged from iterations 5 and 8, so the speed step is the only variable. Watch s-bend max_error against the 0.069 band.
rationale: Iteration 8 (wheel_radius 0.04 m, all else as iteration 5) is the best state so far at 51.13. Progress rose on the s-bend (0.155 to 0.158) and slalom (0.1066 to 0.1075) with max_error held: oval 0.0608, s-bend 0.0684, slalom 0.0634. Iteration 5 showed the same pattern for the 0.030 to 0.035 m step, and iterations 6 and 7 showed that mass 0.5 kg and track 0.14 m both lower progress. Speed (wheel_radius) is therefore the only geometry lever still helping. The s-bend max_error of 0.0684 is close to the 0.069 band, so this step is the last safe one to test. The Builder's geometry is taken exactly: wheel_radius 0.044 m, mass 0.6 kg, wheel_track 0.12 m, body 0.18 x 0.12 m, five sensors at x = -0.03 to 0.03 m, y = 0.04 m, sensor_size 0.012 m. The contract allows wheel_radius up to 0.05 m, so the value is valid. The controller is kept exactly as in iterations 5 and 8 (kp 3.0, ki 0.3, kd 0.1, base_speed 1.6, weights [-2,-1,0,1,2], last_direction). Gains have moved max_error by under 0.007 m in every earlier test, and the Integrator has not seen evidence that a gain change is needed. Changing the gains now would confound the speed test. The risk to watch is that the higher ground speed pushes the s-bend past 0.069, which would show as max_error rising above 0.0684 while progress rises. If that happens, the Builder's fallback is wheel_radius 0.04 m.
